paper.title: Stochastic Multi-Objective Multi-Armed Bandits: Regret Definition and Algorithm

unmapped: Vector-valued rewards with D objectives; regret measured against the Pareto-optimal set (coverage-regret and cumulative adjustment-regret, new definitions)
Learner may pull a set of arms A^t per round
Reward range [0,1] not explicitly stated; Hoeffding's inequality is used in the analysis and experiments use Bernoulli rewards
settings.definition_quote: Given an instance of a MO-MAB problem with \( n \) arms, denoted by \(\mathcal{A}=\{a_1,a_2,...,a_n \}\), and $D$ (maximization) objectives ... In the stochastic setting of the problem \sum_{t=1}^T \mathbf{r}^t(a) = (T \mu_{1}(a), ..., T\mu_{D}(a))

conditions: n < T and D < T (used in proof)

source.label: Coverage Theorem
source.quote: The coverage-regret of algorithm \ref{SMOMABA} is \(R = O\left( T^\frac{2}{3} (n\log T)^\frac{1}{3}\right)\).

results.notes: Coverage-regret (new multi-objective regret notion): for every Pareto-optimal arm, per-objective expected cumulative shortfall. Proof gives 4 T^{2/3}(2 n log T)^{1/3} + small term. By Theorem 4 also valid for efficient PO arms.

source.label: cumulative adjustment-regret Theorem
source.quote: The cumulative adjustment-regret is hold for algorithm \ref{SMOMABA} with the regret \(R = O\left( T^\frac{2}{3} (n\log T)^\frac{1}{3}\right)\).

results.notes: Cumulative adjustment-regret is bounded by |A*| R by definition. Also extended to efficient PO arms in Theorem 4.

source.label: cumulative adjustment-regret Theorem
source.quote: we note that the polynomial-time approximation for the minimum covering set satisfies $|B| \leq \log n \cdot |\mathcal{A}^*|$. Consequently, the polynomial-time algorithm achieves the regret bound of $O\left( \log n \cdot T^{\frac{2}{3}} (n \log T)^{\frac{1}{3}} \right)$ while maintaining correctness.

results.notes: Stated in the proof of Theorem 3 and in the intro; the regret R parameter for the polynomial-time variant (adjustment-regret scaled by |A*|).

source.label: Theorem b_star
source.quote: The regret of the single arm pulling version of Algorithm \ref{SMOMABA} compared to the average best arm $b^*$ is \(R = O\left( T^\frac{2}{3} (n\log T)^\frac{1}{3}\right)\).

results.notes: Regret against a virtual arm b* equal to the average of a diverse set of Pareto-optimal arms; measured as adjustment needed to weakly dominate b*.
